tian (runtime): Quick dump — noticed a regression after merge 3b9f7c. Running microbench with TP=2 PP=2 DP=1 on a 7B-like model. KV cache traffic spikes when prefix_len > 512 and we lose comm/compute overlap. Trace attached.
elaine (perf): can you paste the bench command + raw numbers?
tian (runtime): ran: `python tools/bench_kv.py --model 7b-shard --tp 2 --pp 2 --seq 1024 --batch 1`
logs: `step 1: kv_allreduce 4.2ms, kernel compute 1.1ms, stall 3.1ms; step 50: kv_allreduce 4.8ms`
elaine (perf): wow that's ~4x higher than baseline when PP=1. baseline (TP=2 PP=1) was ~0.9ms for same seq. Do you have nccl profiler traces?
tian (runtime): attached nccl trace: shows repeated small allreduce calls (~256KB chunks) + frequent fallback to ring algo. NVLink lanes saturate and we lose overlap.
samir (infra): likely NCCL algorithm selection is flipping because tensor shapes change with our chunking. If reduce-scatter/allgather are picked we pay extra launches. What are the tensor counts per layer?
tian (runtime): ~48 tensors for KV per layer, chunked into 4 extents each by our kvcache stripe. Per-step we do ~200 collective ops.
dylan (mlops): also remember the batcher: when PP>1 we extend the batching window to keep GPU utilization which increases payload size -> fewer collectives but larger ones. That might push NCCL into less optimal path.
elaine (perf): hypothesis: combo of (a) our kvcache sharding across PP boundaries, (b) batcher increasing payload, (c) kernel selection fallback => extra latency. We should try two experiments: 1) force hierarchical allreduce (intra-node then inter-node), 2) coarsen chunking so fewer allreduces.
tian (runtime): I ran coarse-chunk experiment: set `KVCACHE_CHUNK_SIZE=1MB` -> allreduce count dropped 6x, per-step allreduce latency fell to 1.6ms but peak memory went +200MB. So tradeoff.
samir (infra): that's expected. Another axis: change kvcache placement strategy. If we map KV shards by pipeline-stage affinity (keep local KV for layers resident in a stage) we reduce cross-stage allreduces at the cost of needing to move activations less.
dylan (mlops): TLDR of shard strategies we've considered: [TP-shard: shard across tensor-parallel ranks, good for local KV reads but requires layer-wise collectives], [PP-affinity: KV stays with pipeline stage, avoids per-layer allreduces, but increases activation comm], [DP-replicate-hot: replicate small hot prefixes across DP replicas to avoid collectives for common prefixes].
elaine (perf): can we do a hybrid? For example: PP-affinity for older layers (long KV history) + TP-striping for attention-heavy layers. That reduces freq of allreduces while keeping payloads small.
tian (runtime): implemented a quick prototype: `--kvcache-shard-policy=hybrid-affinity` that picks per-layer policy based on layer index and recent access hotness. Ran short perf: seq=1024, hybrid -> allreduce latency 1.4ms, kernel compute 1.2ms, overlap ~55%.
perf-bot: automated bench summary (2165433000): model=7b, TP=2, PP=2, DP=1, seq=1024, policy=hybrid-affinity, mean_step_ms=12.3, p95_step_ms=18.9.
elaine (perf): promising. Need longer runs (5k steps) to catch JIT/kernel warmup effects and regression windows. Also check quantized kernels: quantized matmul seems to trigger different NCCL shapes.
samir (infra): I'll try forcing NCCL envs: `NCCL_ALGO=ring; NCCL_TOPO_DUMP=1; NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` and test. Maybe toggling `NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0/1` helps for multi-node.
dylan (mlops): one more note: batcher heuristics should be topology-aware. If we detect PP>1, prefer smaller batching window and higher concurrency to keep collectives small but overlapped. I'll sketch a change: cap batch_window = max(8, floor(ideal / pp_stages)).
tian (runtime): action items: 1) I will open PR with hybrid-affinity flag + default coarse chunking for PP>1. 2) elaine runs 5k step benchmark with quantized kernels. 3) samir will sweep NCCL envs on infra cluster. 4) dylan will prototype topology-aware batcher cap.
elaine (perf): add test cases to perf-suite: (A) TP2 PP2 DP1 seq=512/1024/2048, (B) hot-prefix replicate vs hybrid, (C) quantized vs fp16 kernels.
tian (runtime): noted. If anyone sees weird per-layer stalls, post kernel traces (nvprof/ncu) and the `kvcache_stats` timeline. :thumbsup:
